guideTitle: The Best Thunderbolt 4 Docking Stations, and When a USB-C Dock Will Do
metaDescription: Only some docks sold for Thunderbolt 4 ports are Thunderbolt certified. We compared seven, from certified Thunderbolt 4 and 5 docks to DisplayLink alternatives, on displays, charging and ports.
introParagraphs: A Thunderbolt 4 port accepts many docks, but only certified Thunderbolt 4 docks are tested to Intel's requirements for bandwidth, displays and daisy-chaining. In this guide, two docks are Thunderbolt 4 certified (Plugable TBT-UDM, Dell SD25TB4) and one is Thunderbolt 5; the other four are USB-C or DisplayLink docks that also work from a Thunderbolt port.

Those alternatives aren't worse by default. DisplayLink docks can drive three displays from laptops that natively support fewer, at the cost of a driver and some processor load, and USB-C docks can cost less for everyday use.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing. Check your laptop's display support and charger wattage before choosing.

plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-certified.summary: A Thunderbolt 4 certified dock with 100W, dual 4K HDMI or single 6K, 6 USB, SD and Gigabit Ethernet.
plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-certified.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is the straightforward certified Thunderbolt 4 choice: 100W charging, dual 4K over HDMI or a single 6K display, six USB ports, an SD reader and Gigabit Ethernet, driverless on macOS and Windows.

It has fewer display outputs than the Dell, and dual display depends on your laptop's support.
plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-certified.bestFor: Mac or Windows Thunderbolt laptops with two monitors.
plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-certified.skipIf: You use a Dell Pro laptop; the SD25TB4 is designed for it.

dell-pro-tb4-smart-dock-sd25tb4.summary: Dell's certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with 130W, up to 4 displays, 2.5GbE and Wi-Fi.
dell-pro-tb4-smart-dock-sd25tb4.description:
The Dell SD25TB4 is built around Dell's Pro laptops, with 130W charging, support for up to four displays across two DisplayPort 1.4 and HDMI 2.1 outputs, two Thunderbolt 4 ports, 2.5GbE Ethernet and Wi-Fi.

Four displays and full integration depend on a compatible Dell laptop; check Dell's compatibility list.
dell-pro-tb4-smart-dock-sd25tb4.bestFor: Dell Pro laptops, including higher-power models.
dell-pro-tb4-smart-dock-sd25tb4.skipIf: You don't use Dell; the Plugable is the brand-neutral choice.

anker-prime-tb5-dl-docking-station.summary: A 14-in-1 Thunderbolt 5 dock with 140W charging, up to 8K output and active cooling.
anker-prime-tb5-dl-docking-station.description:
The Anker Prime TB5 is a Thunderbolt 5 dock, up to 120Gbps, with 140W charging, up to 8K output with dual display support and active cooling. On a Thunderbolt 4 laptop it runs at Thunderbolt 4 speeds.

It costs considerably more than the Thunderbolt 4 docks at the time of writing; it's worth considering if your next laptop will have Thunderbolt 5.
anker-prime-tb5-dl-docking-station.skipIf: You'll stay on Thunderbolt 4; the Plugable costs much less.

anker-prime-160w-14-port-docking-station.summary: A 14-port dock with 160W total output, dual 4K, 10Gbps data, Ethernet and audio; not Thunderbolt certified.
anker-prime-160w-14-port-docking-station.description:
The Anker Prime 14-port works from a Thunderbolt 4 port but isn't Thunderbolt certified. It offers 14 ports, 160W total output shared across devices, dual 4K, 10Gbps data, Ethernet and audio.

It costs less than the certified docks at the time of writing. It lacks certified Thunderbolt bandwidth and daisy-chaining.
cons: Laptop charging limited by USB PD
anker-prime-160w-14-port-docking-station.bestFor: Many USB peripherals without Thunderbolt devices.
anker-prime-160w-14-port-docking-station.skipIf: You use Thunderbolt drives or displays; a certified dock suits that.

plugable-usb-c-triple-display-100w.summary: A USB-C dock with 100W and three displays: one 4K at 30Hz and two 1080p at 60Hz.
plugable-usb-c-triple-display-100w.description:
The Plugable triple-display dock drives three monitors with 100W charging and six 5Gbps USB ports, and supports Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.

Its display split is one 4K at 30Hz and two 1080p at 60Hz, so it suits three modest monitors better than 4K screens. It isn't Thunderbolt certified.
plugable-usb-c-triple-display-100w.skipIf: You want three 4K 60Hz displays; the Anker DL7400 offers that.

plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-triple-monito.summary: A 13-in-1 DisplayLink dock with triple HDMI, 100W, Ethernet and SD; driver required on Mac.
plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-triple-monito.description:
The Plugable UD-ULTCDL uses DisplayLink to drive three HDMI displays, including from Macs that natively support fewer, with 100W charging, a 20W USB-C output, Gigabit Ethernet, an SD reader and four more USB ports.

It needs the DisplayLink driver on Mac, which adds some processor load and is less suited to video playback of protected content or gaming.
plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-triple-monito.bestFor: Macs that need more monitors than they support natively.
plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-triple-monito.skipIf: Your laptop supports your monitors natively; the Plugable TBT-UDM avoids the driver.

anker-prime-dl7400-14-port-triple-displa.summary: A 14-port DisplayLink dock with triple 4K at 60Hz, 140W output and a cooling fan.
anker-prime-dl7400-14-port-triple-displa.description:
The Anker Prime DL7400 drives three 4K displays at 60Hz through DisplayLink, which is uncommon, with 140W total output, a built-in cooling fan and a display status indicator.

Anker lists it for Windows laptops with the latest DisplayLink driver installed. It isn't Thunderbolt certified.
anker-prime-dl7400-14-port-triple-displa.skipIf: You use a Mac; the Plugable UD-ULTCDL lists Mac support.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Certified Thunderbolt 4 docks (Plugable TBT-UDM, Dell SD25TB4) guarantee bandwidth and daisy-chaining; others work but without those assurances.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Check display needs against your laptop
buyingCriteria.explanation: Native docks can't exceed your laptop's display limit; DisplayLink docks can, with a driver.
Charging here runs from 100W to 140W; compare with your laptop's charger.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Consider Thunderbolt 5 only for the future
buyingCriteria.explanation: On a Thunderbolt 4 laptop, a Thunderbolt 5 dock runs at Thunderbolt 4 speeds.

faq.q: Is every dock that fits a Thunderbolt port a Thunderbolt dock?
faq.a: No. Many USB-C and DisplayLink docks work from a Thunderbolt port without Thunderbolt certification.
It matters most for Thunderbolt storage, displays and daisy-chaining. For basic peripherals, a USB-C dock can suffice.

faq.q: Can I run three monitors from a Mac?
faq.a: Depending on the chip, often only via DisplayLink, as with the Plugable UD-ULTCDL.
Only if you'll use a Thunderbolt 5 laptop; otherwise it runs at Thunderbolt 4 speeds.
Yes, the DisplayLink driver must be installed.

bottomLine: For a certified Thunderbolt 4 dock, the Plugable TBT-UDM is the brand-neutral choice and the Dell SD25TB4 the pick for Dell Pro laptops, with 130W and up to four displays.

For three monitors, the DisplayLink docks are the route: the Plugable UD-ULTCDL for Macs, the Anker DL7400 for three 4K screens on Windows. The Anker Prime TB5 is only worth it with a Thunderbolt 5 laptop in view.
